stories.headline: One Dead, Several Hurt on Goliath Rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia
stories.summary:
One person died and several others were injured in an incident on a rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles from Atlanta. The Cobb County Police Department said it was investigating the fatality. Police did not name the ride, but aerial footage showed the Goliath coaster stopped midway while workers helped riders off.

Officials have not said how the person died or how the others were hurt, and the victim has not been identified. Witnesses told local outlet 11 Alive that a man came loose from his seat, struck the coaster and other riders, and fell onto the roof of a nearby haunted house attraction. A couple said park workers had checked their harnesses before the ride began. The BBC has not verified these accounts.

Six Flags said it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident" and is cooperating with the investigation. The company also said it temporarily closed similar attractions across its parks "out of an abundance of caution." Goliath opened in 2006, stands 200 feet tall, and reaches speeds of up to 70 mph.

The death comes weeks after a Six Flags park in southern California said it would close the X2 coaster after more than 100 people alleged brain injuries from riding it. Six Flags said that ride had passed safety tests but was being retired because it was "the right thing to do." Six Flags is North America's largest amusement park operator, with 20 amusement parks.

stories.headline: Ex-President Joseph Kabila Named Leader of New DR Congo Rebel Coalition
stories.summary:
Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila has been named leader of a new rebel coalition seeking to oust the government of President Felix Tshisekedi. The Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) said it would coordinate "resistance forces" to end "tyranny" and would pursue that goal "by all means, including force." The group was unveiled Monday at a press conference at Kabila's residence in Goma, the largest city in eastern DR Congo, which M23 rebels have controlled since last year.

The announcement is the clearest sign yet of Kabila's direct involvement in an armed movement, a year after he was sentenced to death in absentia for treason. He had previously denied links to M23. M23 leader Sultani Makenga will serve as one of Kabila's four deputies, and the other three also come from the AFC-M23 alliance.

The launch followed a speech days earlier in which Kabila accused Tshisekedi's government of ignoring his peace proposals, undermining constitutional rule, mismanaging the economy and making arbitrary arrests of opponents and officers. The government has not commented publicly on the coalition or the accusations.

Kabila ruled from 2001 until January 2019, when Tshisekedi took office after a disputed election. The two were once allies before falling out, and Kabila went into exile in 2023 before returning to Goma last year. More than 100 militia groups operate in eastern DR Congo. The UN and Western governments accuse Rwanda of backing M23, which Rwanda denies. Tshisekedi said in May that elections due in 2028 might not be held because of the conflict.

stories.headline: Hungarian Parliament Scraps Orban-Era Anti-LGBTQ Measures as EU Releases Frozen Funds
stories.summary:
Hungary's parliament voted Tuesday to amend child protection laws, scrapping measures that stigmatized gay and transgender people. The 2021 Child Protection Law, passed by Viktor Orban's Fidesz majority, banned the "portrayal or promotion of homosexuality or transgenderism" and affected laws on education and assembly. LGBTQ and human rights activists welcomed the change but called for further reforms of Orban-era laws.

The vote is part of a package of laws from the government of Prime Minister Peter Magyar, whose Tisza party won in April and holds the same two-thirds majority Fidesz once had. Minutes after the vote, Budapest said the EU had agreed to release 4.2bn euros in funds frozen during the last years of the Fidesz government. The European Commission had said last month that Hungary addressed a number of rule-of-law breaches affecting the EU budget, and urged readmitting it to Erasmus+ and Horizon Europe.

Tamas Dombos of the Hatter Society said his group had fought the law for five years, though he said problems remain and "we are still knocking on a closed door" on other issues. Magyar's party has softened the legislation without presenting itself as fully liberal on equality, and he avoided gay and transgender rights during his campaign for fear of alienating right-wing voters. Child protection had been central to both parties' images, and it became a liability for Orban after his government supported the pardon of a children's home official who covered up abuse.

stories.headline: Super El Nino Sets New Records, Strengthening to 'Unprecedented Levels'
stories.summary:
El Nino has continued to strengthen to what some scientists call "unprecedented levels," weeks before its expected peak in December. Australia's Bureau of Meteorology said average weekly sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific have reached their highest level on record. This follows a record daily sea surface temperature in the central-eastern Pacific set in September, which exceeded the mark from the very strong 2015 event.

Temperatures above 30C have been recorded for the first time in parts of the tropical Pacific, along with record anomalies and exceptional subsurface warmth. Forecasters in Australia and the US now use a Relative Ocean El Nino Index to account for background ocean warming from climate change. By that measure, current levels exceed the record-breaking December 2015 peak. Dr Zeke Hausfather of Berkeley Earth said, "We are currently witnessing an El Nino event that is unprecedented in the historical record."

The warmth extends well beyond the tropical region normally monitored, and is more widespread than in the 1972-73, 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2015-16 events. The World Meteorological Organization says there is no evidence that climate change is making El Nino events stronger or more frequent, though this remains an active research area. El Nino releases extra ocean heat into the atmosphere, and combined with human-driven warming it is expected to make 2026 one of the warmest years on record, with high temperatures likely to continue into 2027. The most widespread impacts are expected later this year and into 2027.

stories.headline: Update: Ships Sunk in New Drone Attacks Off Bulgaria as Prime Minister Summons Russian Ambassador
stories.summary:
A merchant ship has sunk after drones struck two vessels off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said on Tuesday. One ship went down 17 nautical miles east of Krapets, and one crew member was saved. The second, Ukrainian-owned and Maltese-flagged vessel, the Chelsea 3, was hit by three drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala. All 15 crew were rescued, and five were treated for minor injuries.

Radev convened an emergency security meeting and summoned Russian ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova. He said there was no conclusive evidence of blame on either side, but that "the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation." Mitrofanova reportedly told him she had no information from Russia's defense ministry about the attacks and suggested a third-party provocation. Radev, who took office this summer and has rejected suggestions that he is pro-Russian, said he would speak with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

The attacks follow a similar incident on October 6, when two commercial ships were hit in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. One of them, the Alfa Watan, sank, and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead. Radev had earlier asked NATO and the EU for technical help in investigating those strikes.

Ukraine has directly blamed Russia for the latest attacks. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the Black Sea was becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable." Moscow has not commented publicly. It says it targets ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports, while Kyiv and its European allies say grain and other civilian cargo vessels are being hit.

stories.headline: Update: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia Escalate as Riyadh Airport Death Toll Reaches 13
stories.summary:
The death toll from the Houthi strike on Riyadh's international airport and another facility has risen to 13, according to the latest reporting. Saturday's attack was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since May 2015. US and Saudi officials blame Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, who had not commented on the strike. The Saudi capital was hit by multiple attacks over the weekend.

The strikes come amid escalating fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government. The Houthis have also been fighting pro-government forces over Yemen's Red Sea coast. Security analysts say the group's precision strikes and guerrilla tactics have made it difficult for Saudi forces to gain the upper hand.

BBC analysis says the physical damage from the attacks can be repaired quickly, but the kingdom's reputation for stability is taking a battering. Experts also note that US military assistance, including shuttle tankers and pipelines that bypass the Strait of Hormuz, has allowed Gulf oil exports to rebound.

The attacks sit within the wider US-Iran war and the question of how Washington and Riyadh respond. The Houthi campaign has put new focus on Yemen's long-running civil war, whose humanitarian toll continues to mount.

stories.headline: Katie Zacharia to Hold First White House Press Briefing as New Press Secretary
stories.summary:
Katie Zacharia begins her term as White House press secretary, with an introductory news conference set for Tuesday at 9:30 a.m. President Trump announced the start date on Sunday, saying she would begin on Columbus Day. Her debut ends a weeks-long stretch without a permanent press secretary at the podium.

Zacharia previously worked for one of Trump's companies and built her profile through appearances on conservative-leaning talk shows. Critics note that she has amplified right-wing conspiracy theories. Supporters of the president view her as a loyal communicator who will advance his message directly to the public.

The briefing comes as the Justice Department investigates the five television networks that make up the White House TV press pool, following the suspension of pool coverage. How the new press secretary handles questions on that probe, and on the administration's relationship with the press corps, will be closely watched. The briefing also lands weeks before the midterm elections.

stories.headline: Update: India 'Cockroach' Party Leaders Detained After Entering Barricaded Delhi Protest Site
stories.summary:
Leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party were detained early Tuesday after entering the heavily guarded Jantar Mantar protest site in Delhi. They chanted slogans demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a controversial revision of electoral rolls. Party founder Abhijeet Dipke shared video of Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das being taken away by police after climbing over barricades while holding the Indian flag.

The detentions came a day after the federal home ministry announced that Jantar Mantar would no longer be a designated protest venue, naming three alternative locations where demonstrations can be held with permission. Ranka said the site was de-notified 30 minutes after the party asked police for a protest date. Opponents of Prime Minister Narendra Modi allege the voter list revision benefits his party, a charge it and the Election Commission reject.

Over the weekend, police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists, and closed metro stations amid a heavy deployment of police and paramilitary forces. Opposition parties also marched in Delhi on Monday. The detained leaders said they would not back down.
